Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www_dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 100 s. 2022 September 19, 2022 ATTY. PROSENCIO D. JASO JASO DORILLO & ASSOCIATES Counsel for Victoriano C. Torres Ill Unit 216 Cityland 8 Condominium 98 Sen. Gil Puyat Avenue, Makati City attyjaso@qmail.com Dear Atty. Jaso: This has reference to your letter dated July 27, 2022 requesting that Victoriano C. Torres III should be the one installed and declared as legally entitled to the position of Mayor of the Municipality of Alicia, Province of Bohol. Per the documents referred to the Department, the following are the antecedent facts: The Court of Appeals (Special 20th Division), Cebu City promulgated a Decision dated March 12, 2019 in "People of the Philippines vs. Ayuban, et al., " imposing upon Accused-Appellant Marnilou S. Ayuban, et al. (hereinafter referred to as "Mayor-elect Mamilou Ayuban") the penalty of imprisonment for an indeterminate period of six (6) years and one (1) month, as minimum, to ten (IO) years and six (6) months as maximum, with perpetual disqualification from public office; • Accused-appellants Mamilou Ayuban, et al. filed a Motion for Reconsideration to the aforesaid CA Decision but was denied; The matter was elevated to the Supreme Court via a Petition for Review on Certiorari but the same was unfavorably resolved; Thereafter, a Second Motion for Reconsideration with Motion to Direct Court of Appeals to Remand the Records of the case back to the Regional Trial Court was filed but was also denied for failure to show any reversible error in the assailed judgment; On October 14, 2020, the aforesaid Decision of the Supreme Court became final and executory and was, accordingly, recorded in the Book of Entries of Judgments; Marnilou Ayuban filed his Certificate for Candidacy (COC) in the May 9, 2022 National and Local Elections; Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

• Marnilou Ayuban won as Mayor of Alicia, Bohol and was proclaimed as such; • Meantime, Mayor-elect Marnilou Ayuban, et al. filed before the RTC a Manifestation with Motion to Hold in Abeyance the Issuance of Warrant to Enforce Judgment asking that they be allowed to continue their temporary liberty under their existing bail bonds and for the court to defer the issuance of warrants of arrest against them to enforce the final judgment on the ground that they had filed before the Supreme Court on March 30, 2022 a Motion to Elevate the Second Motion for Reconsideration to the Supreme Court En Banc pursuant to Section 3, Rule 15 of the Intemal Rules of the Supreme Court; On June 7, 2022, the Manifestation with Motion was however denied by Hon. Jorge B. Espinal, Presiding Judge, Br. 51 , 7th Judicial Region; • Despite the foregoing, on June 8, 2022, Mayor-elect Marnilou Ayuban took his oath of office; On June 16, 2022, a Warrant of Arrest was issued against Mayor-elect Marnilou Ayuban, among others; • Since June 30, 2022, Mayor-elect Mamilou was not seen physically present in the municipal hall. However, various documents were circulated such as Memorandum Order No. 1, series of 2022 which was purportedly signed by him designating Junavie Piquero, the Local Civil Registrar whom he allegedly appointed as Municipal Administrator, as Officer-in-Charge as he was supposedly on a leave of absence; There were also verbal reports that Mayor-elect Mamilou Ayuban conducted a meeting with municipal functionaries through a virtual platform and allegedly revoked the designation of Junavie Piquero as OIC; On May 17, 2022, Mr. Torres III filed a Petition for Quo Warranto against Ms. Ayuban before RTC, 7th Judicial Region, Branch 51, Carmen, Bohol on the ground that Mr. Ayuban committed material misrepresentation when he stated in Item II of her COC that he is eligible to run for public office and in Item 22 when he stated under oath that he was not found guilty by final and executory judgment for an offense which carries with it the accessory penalty of perpetual disqualification to hold public office; On July 15, 2022, RTC Branch 51 granted the petition for Quo Warranto and found that Mr. Ayuban committed material misrepresentation. The Court further ruled that the subsequent proclamation of Ms. Ayuban as elected Mayor of Alicia is declared null and void and order the COMELEC to constitute a Special Municipal Board of Canvassers to proclaim Mr. Victoriano C. Torres III as the duly elected Mayor of Alicia, Bohol; On July 18, 2022, DILG-Region VII issued a communication, pertinent portion of which reads-. Page 2 of 5

"It may be observed that the last paragraph of the aforequoted provision enumerated the specific causes of permanent vacancies. Such enumeration was followed by a general statement, to wit: "... is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office". This general state statement may refer to permanent vacancies brought about by application of laws, such as perpetual disqualification to hold public office as an accessory penalty in criminal conviction, such as in the case of Mayor-Elect Ayuban. A criminal conviction carries with it certain inherent accessory penalties which operate as a disqualification from holding public office. As stated in the narration of facts above, the decision convicting Mayor Elect Ayuban has already become final and executory. The finality of said Decision would warrant the application of accessory penalties. x x x x x Otherwise stated, these accessory penalties that are inherent to the penalty imposed upon Mayor —Elect Ayuban, would permanently incapacitate him from further discharging the functions of his office. Including that of signing official documents appurtenant to the Office of the Mayor. Such permanent incapacity on the part of the Mayor-Elect Ayuban will thus give rise to the existence of a permanent vacancy in the Office of the Mayor. There being a permanent vacancy in the Office of the Mayor, you, as the Vice-Mayor thereat shall become the mayor applying the aforequoted provision of Section 44 of the Local Government Code of 1991 ." In your letter dated July 27, 2022, you wrote the DILG Secretary saying that DILG-Region VII Director Leocadio Trovela committed an egregious error in holding that Vice-Mayor Cesy Balahay "shall be come Mayor". You are of the view that Victoriano Torres III was the only eligible candidate for the position of Mayor in Alicia, Bohol citing: (1) Section 40 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 which disqualifies a person sentenced by final judgment for an offense involving moral turpitude or for an offense punishable by one (1) year or more of imprisonment, within two (2) tears after serving sentence from running for any elective local position, and (2) jurisprudence holding that conviction by final judgment, with the penalty of prision mayor, disqualifies a candidate perpetually from holding any public office, or from being elected to any public office. In the same letter, you are requesting the DILG Secretary "xxx that, Victoriano C. Torres III be installed and declared as legally entitled to the position of Mayor of the Municipality of Alicia, Province of Bohol. " • In a letter dated July 27, 2022, DILG-Region VII Director Leocadio Trovela indorsed to the Central Office the letter from Vice-Mayor Cesyl Balahay requesting for the issuance of a directive that he can now assume as the Municipal Mayor of Alicia, Bohol; Page 3 of 5

• PD Jerome G. Gonzales issued on August 4, 2022 a Certification, pertinent portion of which reads: "This is to certify that per records on file in this office, HON. CESYL L— BALAHAY is the incumbent Mayor of the Municipality of Alicia, Bohol after she assume office by succession on August 3, 2022." Please be informed that the communication of RD Trovela dated July 18, 2022 declaring the existence of a permanent vacancy in the Office of the Mayor was issued without knowing of the RTC's decision on the Petition for Quo Warranto. The advice is in consonance with the facts available at the time of its issuance and the declaration of vacancy was in accordance with the circumstances provided under the Local Govemment Code. Such was done to prevent paralysis of government operations. However, the aforesaid guidance rendered by DILG Region VII has become moot and inapplicable in light of the subsequent events that took place. Nevertheless, considering that the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) has jurisdiction over issues and cases arising from the national and local elections, this Department will defer to their wisdom to settle the issue on who is the rightful Mayor of Alicia, Bohol. Likewise, this Level is requesting the Commission's guidance relative to the ruling of RTC Branch 51 as well the final and executory decision of the criminal case filed against Mayor Ayuban Pending guidance from the COMELEC and the final disposition of the Petition for Quo Warranto, this Department is constrained to declare a temporary vacancy in the Office of the Mayor to prevent hiatus and paralysis in the government operations. Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides for the procedure in filling in the temporary vacancy in the office of the Local Chief Executive, to wit: SECTION 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. — (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor. citv or municipal vice-mayor. the highest rankinq sangguniang baranqay member shall automaticallv exercise the powers and perform the duties and fuoction#. of the local chief exequtive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (3()) working days. Hence, for the meantime, the duly elected Vice-Mayor, Hon. Cesyl L. Balahay, shall sit as Acting Mayor by virtue of automatic succession. Meanwhile, the highest Sangguniang Bayan Member, Marciano S. Ayuban, Jr., pursuant to Administrative Page 4 of S

Order No. 151 per designation by the Secretary of DILG, shall sit as Acting Vice- Mayor. Relatively, we regret to inform you that this Department cannot grant the request of your client without proper guidance from the COMELEC. The foregoing is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have addressed your concem accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: NGAN tary for Local Government Unde OUSLG/MLVLLLS-LRALLD/c1p,'OD copy DIRECTOR LEOCADIO T.
